pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School, Camden’s only maintained nursery, provides high quality Early Years education in the heart of historic Bloomsbury. Led by a specialist head teacher and a team of qualified teachers and experienced Early Years practitioners, we have consistently been rated ‘Outstanding’ by Ofsted since 2012.
Our site, and its immediate surroundings, has been a special place for children since the foundation of the Foundling Hospital in 1739. Today the children in our care benefit from not only two airy and attractive wings of purpose-built classrooms, but also a large, well-resourced playground and landscaped garden.
We offer places for children aged two to five, and are open 8.30am-5.30pm, 44 weeks a year. Our intake reflects the diverse community we serve. Inclusion is at the forefront of our philosophy: we positively welcome children of all abilities, including those with ‘Special Education Needs and Disabilities’.
Play is central to our approach to learning and development. ‘A child’s greatest achievements,’ observed Russian psychologist Lev Vygotsky, ‘are possible in play.’ In partnership with our parents, we provide a positive environment in which, with the encouragement and guidance of staff, each child can have fun and flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Parent Partnership
pageCache.text:
Parent Partnership
Working in partnership with parents and carers is central to our work at Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School. Research shows that involving parents and carers in their children’s learning is the most important factor in enabling children to do well. Parents are children’s first and most enduring educators.
Parents are encouraged to be actively involved in their child’s learning at nursery. We run termly workshops about various aspects of learning and development in the ‘Parents’ Room’ so that parents can learn what we do to support their child. Parents and carers are also encouraged to get involved in annual cultural events such as ‘Black History Month’ or our community day, a fun-filled, fundraising jamboree which concludes the summer term.
Parents are also encouraged to speak to their child’s ‘key person’ as much as possible. Each ‘key person’ has a central role in not only igniting a child’s enthusiasm for learning but also in helping each child to both thrive individually and form respectful relationships with others. Brief, informal parental feedback is available at pick-up. Once a term, parents are invited to discuss progress with their child’s ‘key person’ with reference to their child’s profile book. A written report is completed at end-of-stage and end-of-school transition.
Where there are concerns about a child, we work closely with parents and carers and, if necessary, outside agencies to give the children in our care the best support possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Governors
pageCache.text:
Governors
Our governing body, whose responsibilities are undertaken on an unpaid, voluntary basis, is responsible for strategic oversight of educational performance, financial management and regulatory compliance.
The current governing body is made up of the Head teacher plus staff, local authority, community and parent governors, all of whom are committed to working tirelessly on the school’s behalf. Our governors do not have any business or financial interests which may impact on their role nor are they governors at other schools unless stated.
Oversight of school business is undertaken in a Full Governing Body meeting twice a term. Members provide oversight and scrutiny of the school’s safeguarding, academic standards, budget, and health and safety. Minutes of meetings are available on request at the school office.
Positions for the governing body come up on a regular basis, and applications are warmly encouraged. If you are interested in becoming a governor at the school, please contact the school office for further information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
We follow the ‘Early Years Foundation Stage’ (EYFS), a statutory framework that sets out the standards for learning, development and care of children from birth to five years old. Of the seven areas of learning and development in the EYFS, the key generic areas of learning are personal, social and emotional development, physical development and communication and language.
Our approach to learning is child-centred and play-based. Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget spoke of play as ‘the work of childhood’. Through play, children develop language skills, creativity, and advance socially and intellectually. A ‘playful’ approach to learning builds on children’s interests, existing knowledge and experiences.
Central to the learning and wellbeing of each child is their ‘key person’ who, through ongoing observations, makes informed decisions about how best to support learning and development. ‘Profile books’, which parents are welcome to browse at any time, contain observations and annotated examples of work.
The EYFS promotes ‘partnership working’ between school and families to ensure the best start possible for children. There is time to talk briefly to your child’s ‘key person’ at drop-off and collection. More extended meetings to discuss the children and their progress occur regularly throughout the year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Equality, Diversity & Inclusion
pageCache.text:
Equality, Diversity & Inclusion
As a school that serves a diverse community in central London, we are committed to supporting and promoting equality, diversity and inclusion, and ensuring these principles are embedded in everything we do. We want the children in our care to be given every opportunity to develop to their full potential and maximise their chances of success in all areas of life.
A number of whole-school initiatives convey positive messages about equality, inclusion and diversity, and promote community cohesion. Festivals such as Chinese New Year, Diwali and Eid are genuine celebrations of our multi-faith, multi-cultural intake. Themed topics such as ‘Black History Week’ are embedded into an inclusive curriculum – not tokenistic gestures of support.
From our intake to our infrastructure, equality of opportunity is at the heart of everything we do. The achievements of Black, Asian and ethnic minorities are celebrated throughout the year. To promote a cross-curricular sense of inclusivity, we strive to ensure that our curriculum reflects the diversity of race, gender and sexuality seen in contemporary Britain.
Working in partnership with families, we strive to meet the diverse needs of children who experience barriers to learning by providing outstanding support within the school and accessing, where necessary, a range of external agencies. As a school, we are committed to ensuring that every child in our care can thrive, irrespective of difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas Coram Centre and Nursery School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
‘Forest School’ is a progressive educational approach inspired by the Scandinavian ‘open air life’ ethos which, since 1993, has promoted a play-based model of learning outdoors. We whole-heartedly support this encouragement of an active and healthy outdoors lifestyle in children.
Under the leadership of our Forest School co-ordinators, ‘Kinder’ children (in the company of their ‘key person’ and parents) are given the opportunity to visit Collingham Gardens, conveniently located within the Coram Campus itself. Although a small space, there are plenty of minibeasts to seek out!
In their sessions the children are encouraged to see the extraordinary in the everyday: to notice colours, shapes and patterns in trees, flowers and vegetables, to become more aware of the weather, and to think about the influence of the seasons on living things.
The exploratory approach of ‘Forest School’ very much informs how we work with the children on-site, too. Research shows that a regular appreciation of nature helps children develop socially, emotionally, physically and linguistically. Given our central London location, we are especially keen to instil a sense of wonder and curiosity in the natural world.
